title: The global operator is triangulated in the coefficient
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ a cohomological correspondence as in [def-trf-correspondence]. Assume $c_2$ is proper and $c$ is admissible: $c_1$ and each base change of $c_1$ used in the construction are exceptionally admissible at $A$ in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility], using the constructible exceptional adjoint. Let $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ be the bounded constructible finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the small pro-etale site, and let
$K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and let $(u',u,u'')$ be a morphism of the
corresponding triangles of the functors $Lc_2^*$ and $Rc_1^!$.
Then the global operators of [def-trf-global-operator] fit into a
morphism of distinguished triangles

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
R\Gamma_c(X,K')&\xrightarrow{\ T_c(u')\ }&R\Gamma_c(X,K')\\
\Big\downarrow&&\Big\downarrow\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K)&\xrightarrow{\ T_c(u)\ }&R\Gamma_c(X,K)\\
\Big\downarrow&&\Big\downarrow\\
R\Gamma_c(X,K'')&\xrightarrow{\ T_c(u'')\ }&R\Gamma_c(X,K'').
\end{array}
$$

proof.text:
Write $P=Lc_2^*$, $Q=Rc_1^!$, $H_X=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ and $H_C=R\Gamma_c(C,-)$. By [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $H_V=\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Ra_{V!}$ for $V=X,C$. The finite-Tor category is a full triangulated subcategory by [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated], so the input triangle is distinguished also in $D^b_c(X,A)$. The structure maps $a_V$ are separated finite type and $A=A_{E,n}$ with $\ell
e p$, so [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility] applies to $Ra_{V!}$ as an exact functor on the bounded constructible categories, so the fibre functor can indeed be applied. The finite-stage clause of [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] makes $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ exact. Their composite is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite]. Thus the given triangle $\Delta=(K',K,K'',d_1,d_2,\delta)$ has distinguished image $H_X\Delta$ in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$, with last arrow $h=\chi_{H_X}(K')H_X(\delta)$. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $P$ carries the finite-Tor input objects into $D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$. In the current [def-trf-admissibility], the specified constructible functors $Rc_{1!}:D^b_{ctf}(C,A)	o D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $Q=Rc_1^!:D^b_{ctf}(X,A)	o D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$ are equipped with their natural unit and counit. Applying these two displayed restrictions successively shows that $Q$ and $Rc_{1!}Q$ take the input objects into the respective finite-Tor categories. This uses the constructible adjunction only; the availability of this datum is a theorem for every separated finite-type $c_1$. Thus $H_C$ is defined and shift-commuting on all coefficient objects appearing below, and the $c_1$ counit is a transformation on the stated constructible domain. Use the canonical shifts for $P$ and $Rc_{1!}$, and for $Q$ the canonical composite shift of its defining formula $
u_C^*c_1^{	imes}R
u_{X,*}$; these are the shifts with which the statement forms the image triangles of $P$ and $Q$, so no other shift on $Q$ is chosen.

proof.text:
Separate the five-arrow composite of [def-trf-global-operator] into
$$a:H_X\xrightarrow{H_X\eta_{c_2}}H_XRc_{2*}P\xrightarrow{\alpha_{c_2,P}}H_CP,\qquad b:H_CQ\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Fib}_s(\gamma_{c_1,Q}^{-1})}H_XRc_{1!}Q\xrightarrow{H_X\varepsilon_{c_1}}H_X.$$
The definition specifies $\alpha_{c_2,M}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\gamma_{c_2,M})\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}(p_{c_2,M}^{-1}))$, where $p_{c_2}:Rc_{2!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_{2*}$ is proper coincidence and $\gamma_{c_i}:Ra_{X!}Rc_{i!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{C!}$ is composition for $a_Xc_i=a_C$. Thus the first arrow uses the ordinary unit. Regrouping the defining composite gives $T_c(v)=b_L\circ H_C(v)\circ a_L$ for $v:PL\to QL$.

proof.text: The intermediate objects have the required constructible domains by [lem-trf-global-operator-perfect]: its statement includes every intermediate compact-support complex in the defining composite, not only its endomorphism. Its hypotheses hold for each input $L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$: the correspondence is admissible, $c_2$ is proper, and one may take the zero coefficient map $PL\to QL$ when checking domains independently of $v$. In particular $Rc_{2*}PL$ and $Rc_{1!}QL$ are finite-Tor constructible on $X$, and $PL,QL$ are so on $C$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies bounded etale-origin witnesses for these bounded constructible objects. Consequently all evaluations of the compact-support comparisons below lie in their specified domain.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-finite-structural-maps-commshift] with $f=c_2$, or with $f=c_i$ and $g=a_X$ for composition. Its schemes are separated finite type over $k$, its coefficients are $A=A_{E,n}$, properness holds for $c_2$, and step 3 supplies the etale-origin domain. Clauses (1)--(3), including the inverse-isomorphism assertion, give shift compatibility of $\eta_{c_2}$, $p_{c_2}^{-1}$, $\gamma_{c_2}$ and $\gamma_{c_1}^{-1}$. Clause (4), with $f=c_1$, applies to the specified constructible adjunction and the canonical composite shift of $Q$ fixed in step 1. It gives precisely
$$\varepsilon_{c_1,L[1]}=\varepsilon_{c_1,L}[1]\circ\chi_{Rc_{1!}Q}(L).$$
Thus the exceptional counit is compatible with the shift already used in the hypothesis on $(u',u,u'')$.

source.place: Proof, five-arrow factorization and sentence about natural transformations of exact functors; corrected initial unit

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] on the transformations of step 4. Clause (ii) allows left whiskering by $Ra_{X!}$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_s$, which commute with shifts by step 1; clause (iii) allows right whiskering by $P$ or $Q$, with their specified shifts. Clause (i) then composes the factors defining $a$ and $b$ in step 2. Clause (iv) identifies the composite shifts under these regroupings. Therefore $a:H_X\to H_CP$ and $b:H_CQ\to H_X$ are shift-compatible natural transformations for exactly the image triangles in the statement.

source.place: Proof, five-arrow factorization and sentence about natural transformations of exact functors; corrected initial unit

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism] to $a$ and $b$. It gives morphisms of triangles $a_\Delta:H_X\Delta\to(H_CP)\Delta$ and $b_\Delta:(H_CQ)\Delta\to H_X\Delta$. The hypothesis says that $(u',u,u'')$ is a morphism $P\Delta\to Q\Delta$, including its third square. Applying $H_C$ gives the triple $(H_Cu',H_Cu,H_Cu'')$ as a morphism $(H_CP)\Delta\to(H_CQ)\Delta$. For the third square explicitly, apply $H_C$ to $Q(\delta)u''$ followed by $\chi_Q(K')$, use the given equation with $u'[1]\chi_P(K')P(\delta)$, and use naturality of $\chi_{H_C}$ at $u'$ to replace $\chi_{H_C}(QK')H_C(u'[1])$ by $(H_Cu')[1]\chi_{H_C}(PK')$. This is exactly the triangle-morphism equation for the composite shift isomorphisms. The first two squares follow by applying the functor to the given equalities.

proof.text:
Compose the three triangle morphisms of step 6, whose components are $b_L H_C(u_L)a_L=T_c(u_L)$ by step 2. To display the connecting square without suppressing it, let $h_P,h_Q$ be the last arrows of $(H_CP)\Delta,(H_CQ)\Delta$. The three third-square equations are $h_Pa_{K''}=a_{K'}[1]h$, $h_QH_C(u'')=H_C(u')[1]h_P$ and $hb_{K''}=b_{K'}[1]h_Q$. Hence
$$hT_c(u'')=b_{K'}[1]h_QH_C(u'')a_{K''}=b_{K'}[1]H_C(u')[1]h_Pa_{K''}=T_c(u')[1]h.$$
For the first square, the first component equations of step 6 give
$$H_X(d_1)T_c(u')=b_KH_C(Qd_1)H_C(u')a_{K'}=b_KH_C(u)H_C(Pd_1)a_{K'}=T_c(u)H_X(d_1).$$
For the second square, its second component equations give
$$H_X(d_2)T_c(u)=b_{K''}H_C(Qd_2)H_C(u)a_K=b_{K''}H_C(u'')H_C(Pd_2)a_K=T_c(u'')H_X(d_2).$$ Composition is componentwise by [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]. Both source and target are the distinguished triangle $H_X\Delta$ of step 1, proving the assertion, including the omitted fourth row of the displayed diagram. No invertibility of any $u$ is used.
